reviews.title: Target A: phase-integrated plateau sink surplus
reviews.head: 52a89ded959be4c96db4bdc4622ee73f7f63c3bd

amendment_audit.original_issue_and_repair: The original prose selected a measurable phase-dependent Section-102 basis but did not make the phase-dependent auxiliary perfect matching used by Section 174 part of the selector. Matching-dependent sector sets C_i, O_i, and Xi therefore were not shown measurable by selecting a basis alone. The amended proof fixes one lexicographic order on the finite labelled pairs (B, mu_0), selects the first admissible pair, and explains why each admissibility fiber and the resulting sector counts are Borel.
amendment_audit.corrected_selector_review: For a fixed bounded fundamental cell, the finite source neighborhood and lattice rows give finitely many candidate labelled bases and matchings. Strict incidence/distance conditions and finite rank/matching conditions define Borel admissibility sets; finite lexicographic selection therefore has Borel fibers. The stated Section-102/174 admissibility hypotheses supply a nonempty pair at every generic phase. This makes Xi and the basis-count integrand measurable; they are bounded on the cell, so the translation expectations used in the proof are defined.
amendment_audit.decisive_implication_reconstruction: From Xi=|O_iso|+sum_i(|O_i|-|C_i|)_+, obtain Xi >= |O|-|T_O|-sum_i|C_i| using the stated exterior-sink partition. With |C^partial|=m*-|Z|-d_int and sum_i|C_i|=|C^partial|-t_Sigma, plus T_Z disjoint-union T_O=T_Sigma, derive Xi-j*-|T_Z| >= |O|+|Y_0|+|Z|-|T_Sigma|-N+d_int+t_Sigma. Translation averaging gives E|Z|=area(K*)/a0, E(|O|+|Y_0|)=(area(K*+tB)-area(K*))/a0, and E|T_Sigma|=A_Sigma/a0. This reconstructs the displayed inequality (1). The residual is integer-valued; if no generic phase has residual >=0, its mean is <=-1. Thus any strict lower bound >-1 forces one phase with Xi>=j*+|T_Z|. Substituting A_Sigma<=pi+2e yields the stated sufficient criterion (2). The implication is valid under the cited Section-102/174/175 and actual-response hypotheses.

reviews.title: Target A: geometric full-shore extension regression
reviews.head: 7f4dac815680da2b8ad6b0623369aeab3a730978

amendment_audit.original_issue_and_repair: The original README claimed a 5x5 Cartesian unit grid centered at x was contained in H by comparing its radius squared 8 to the hexagon's inradius squared 27, while the checker actually constructed the Cartesian grid about the origin. The amendment aligns prose and checker: it records x=(1/2,sqrt(3)/6) in Cartesian coordinates, |x|^2=1/3, |g|^2<=8, then uses |g-x|<sqrt(8)+1<4<3sqrt(3), with 16<27. The checker now verifies each exact premise of this triangle-inequality containment certificate.
amendment_audit.decisive_implication_reconstruction: In triangular coordinates q(u,v)=u^2+uv+v^2 is the exact squared Euclidean metric. The eleven sources (five local labels plus six regular-hexagon vertices) have minimum pairwise q=13/12>1; local sources lie within radius 3sqrt(3) of x, and the six vertices have hull H, so A is unit-separated, triangle-free, contained in H, and K+B subset H. The complete lattice shore for K={x} is {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}; the coordinate completing-square bound makes the finite enumeration exhaustive. The selected full-shore matchings are valid and the three Y-matching segments are pairwise disjoint. Restricting to C={x}, O={y0}, the selected pair both maps to a1, giving overlap 1; alternate strict conflicts x-a2 and y0-a3 use distinct labels, giving achievable overlap 0. A coordinated alternative pair of full-shore matchings also attains zero, so this disproves only the universal claim that arbitrary inherited full-shore choices preserve the restricted minimum. Separately, the 25-point Cartesian grid is unit-separated and lies in the inscribed disk of H, proving alpha_1(H)>=25>|A|=11. Thus the fixture is not the Section-168 zero-slack endpoint.
